name: fstubner/agent-skills
_defaultSkillNote: Not a pipeline head — every skill below fires independently on its own trigger. This is only the suggested starting point when a request is greenfield/ambiguous and no single skill's trigger clearly applies yet.
_harnessPathsNote: Claude Desktop reads the same ~/.claude/skills as Claude Code (confirmed, no separate entry needed) and has no filesystem target for cloud use — see INSTALL.md. Codex's skill directory is genuinely unsettled upstream as of mid-2026: OpenAI's own skill-installer/skill-creator tools still default to ~/.codex/skills, current public docs point to ~/.agents/skills instead, and there are open OpenAI GitHub issues (openai/codex#28505, openai/skills#420) showing the Codex Desktop app failing to discover skills placed in ~/.agents/skills. Installing to BOTH paths (a value can be an array) is a deliberate hedge against that instability, not an assumption either one is settled — revisit once upstream converges. Antigravity CLI specifically reads ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills; a broader Antigravity-product-wide path (~/.gemini/config/skills) was also reported but is not what the CLI itself was confirmed to read.

skills.role: Dispatcher — routes a greenfield/ambiguous request to whichever skills apply
Reasoning lens catalog + triage guide + four named mindsets
Test pyramid triage, behavior over implementation, flaky-test discipline
Schema design — keys, normalization, nullability, migrations
CLI surface + contract — naming, config precedence, exit codes, dry-run
CI/CD pipeline gating, deployment strategy, rollback
Turn a correction or confirmation into a durable rule/fixture/memory
Evidence-first codebase audit — severity-ranked findings, coverage gaps stated
Multi-agent topology, delegation contracts, governance, failure recovery

artifacts._requiredHeadingsNote: Was the only acceptance-gated document with no content requirement, so existence was the whole check and a file containing 'TODO' passed the gate (probe, 2026-08-02). These match frontend/assets/ux-walkthrough.md's own sections, so a filled-in template satisfies them by construction.

artifacts.note: Written only when the stack was open to choose (frontend/SKILL.md). Not acceptance-gated: an existing-stack project legitimately has no stack-decision.md.
Consumed directly by frontend's own checker (F-tokens-contrast), which is itself acceptance-gated via frontend-report. Listed here so it isn't undocumented, not double-gated.

Shotgun surgery read from git history. Not acceptance-gated: it describes how a codebase has CHANGED, which a fresh project legitimately has no data for, and a ship decision should not hinge on commit-history volume. Review-time signal, recorded so it is not undocumented.
Invoked directly via its own CLI (targets as positional args, optional --report <path>), not through --root/evidenceDir like the registry-driven checkers. No default file: null reflects that.

Invoked directly via its own CLI (--root <dir>, optional --strict/--report), self-contained like ai-prose-slop's check-prose.js. Only checks circular imports (O-circular-deps) — the one code-organization rule that's genuinely deterministic; everything else in that skill stays judgment-only.

Invoked directly via its own CLI (--root <dir>, optional --strict/--report). Checks file size (any language) and nesting depth (brace-delimited languages only, excluding Go) — the two code-smells rules genuinely checkable without a per-language parser; everything else in that skill stays judgment-only.

Invoked directly via its own CLI (--root <dir>, optional --strict/--report). Checks ONLY raw .sql migration files for destructive drops, unsafe NOT NULL additions, renames, and volatile-function column defaults — every check id is prefixed DM-sql- specifically so this is never mistaken for having evaluated data modeling generally. A project modeling data via an ORM schema DSL or a NoSQL store gets none of this checked mechanically; SKILL.md's judgment rules still apply to those, just without a script behind them.
